messages:
acct-42: our app started seeing a big p99 spike on /v1/fn-call this morning, latency went from ~120ms to ~850ms, p95 also up. Any idea? :grimacing:
maya_support: sorry to hear that — can you share a request id or sample payload? are you using structured output + tool router?
acct-42: yes, we recently turned on strict JSON schema validation for tool responses. sample req id: rq_20260317_9b3
maya_support: thanks. do you have a repro curl?
acct-42: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/fn-call -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-XXX' -d '{"model":"rwd-qa-1","input":"getUser(123)","tools":["db","http"]}'
jorge_runtime: tagging in eng-runtime. maya, priya — initial hunch: schema validation in the router is running synchronously and doing full JSON.parse + ajv.validate per tool output which can amplify serialization cost for multi-tool flows. that would blow up p99 for short requests.
priya_ml: we benchmarked ajv earlier; naive validation on large nested outputs can add 200-400ms per validation on cpu-bound instances, esp if response objects are large. if the router validates every tool output inline, it compounds.
ethan_oncall: I'm seeing correlated logs around 07:12-07:30 UTC for rq_20260317_9b3, worker pod rrt-12 had CPU saturation. snippet from runtime logs: 
```
[t=07:12:19.432] rpc: recv fn output size=23kb
[t=07:12:19.433] router: validating tool output (schema=order.v2.json)
[t=07:12:20.105] router: validation complete (duration=672ms)
[t=07:12:20.106] rpc: dispatch to downstream
```
maya_support: that 672ms validation matches the p99s. acct-42, can you temporarily disable strict schema validation from your integration to confirm? there's a per-client toggle in the dashboard under "tooling -> validation".
acct-42: disabled it for a subset of traffic (10%) around 07:45. p99 dropped back to ~180ms for the sampled bucket. confirmed.
jorge_runtime: ok confirmed root cause: synchronous ajv validation in the router. proposed mitigations: 1) make validation async/background with optimistic accept and attach validation result as a background job; 2) add fast-path for small schemas / primitive outputs to skip heavy compile; 3) cache compiled validators per schema version (we might not be caching aggressively); 4) offload heavy validation to separate worker pool (cpu-nice).
priya_ml: also suggest using schema compilation (ajv.compile) at model load time rather than per-request; plus consider switching to a faster validator (ajv with optimize) or using webassembly-compiled validator.
ethan_oncall: short-term mitigation for customers: a per-tenant flag to disable inline validation (we already used it), and an auto-fallback to a lighter schema check that only type-checks top-level fields.
maya_support: i've created a ticket SUP-5379 and flagged as high-severity; adding eng-runtime and infra. acct-42 we've rolled back the feature for your workspace and increased routing capacity while we patch. apologies for the impact.
jorge_runtime: working on a code change to cache compiled validators and make validation off-main-thread. plan: patch in next release window (rollout canary next Thurs). I'll post PR and perf numbers.
priya_ml: i'll run microbenchmarks to quantify p50/p95/p99 impact of compiled vs uncompiled validation and include memory/CPU cost.
ethan_oncall: for immediate monitoring: creating a dashboard showing validation duration histogram per schema id, and an alert for median > 100ms or p99 > 400ms.
maya_support: acct-42 can you confirm if any billing anomalies came with the spike? we saw extra CPU usage but want to check cost impact for you.
acct-42: we saw ~18% higher infra cost for that window, not catastrophic but noticeable. thanks for the quick rollback.
jorge_runtime: notes for the fix: avoid JSON.stringify/parse duplication, reuse parsed objects, compile validators once and memoize with LRU keyed by schema hash + version, and add a runtime flag to run in async validate mode. also consider streaming validation for huge outputs.
maya_support: i'll keep you posted on the timeline. please add any repro steps in SUP-5379. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
